title: Microsoft Copilot: add agents and skills from the plus menu
summary: Hold: Microsoft documents preview automation for both access settings that the briefing reports as having no API. The prose also casts doubt on User access governing the agents and plugins reached through the new menu, although Microsoft says that setting applies to all agents and plugins.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Scope; Governance controls: first row
claims.claim: Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Settings > User access reaches the user and group access control.
claims.quote: Open the Microsoft 365 admin center in your browser. ... Select Agents > Settings > User access to manage your organization's agents and plugins.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls: first row API
claims.claim: No API or automation is documented for User access.
claims.quote: These resources also support remediation and applyOnce. ... userAssignmentCategory ... Specifies whether all users or no users can access agents and plugins. ... everyone, noOne
claims.fix: Replace controls[0].api null with kind 'graph', call 'POST /beta/admin/configurationManagement/configurationMonitors', docs 'https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/configurationmanagement-post-configurationmonitors?view=graph-rest-beta'. Add to its note: 'Preview, global service only. Set mode=applyOnce and baseline.resources to resourceType microsoft.agent.useraccess, resourceVersion 1; properties.valueObject.userAssignmentCategory accepts everyone or noOne. This schema does not document specific-group assignment. Requires delegated ConfigurationMonitoring.ReadWrite.All for the caller, delegated CopilotPolicySettings.ReadWrite for the TCM service principal, and AI Administrator for the signed-in user.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/utcm-agent-resources and https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/utcm-remediation-applyonce-resources; update the rendered API cell consistently.
